specs.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / photorealistic-natural interior visualization.
Image 1 is the edit target AND THE ONLY SPATIAL ANCHOR: a genuine 360-degree by 180-degree equirectangular spherical panorama of this user's current home, not a conventional flat wide-angle photograph.
Image 2 is the user's selected STYLE reference (a screenshot of the preferred living-room photo). Image 3 is a clean higher-resolution companion from that selected photo set. Transfer their photographic realism, natural sunlight, tactile materials, and restrained modern Japanese visual character. Do not copy the screenshot UI, crop, room geometry or camera from images 2/3.
PRIMARY REQUIREMENT: a convincing architectural interior photograph IN A FULL SPHERICAL PANORAMA FORMAT. Upgrade the plastic-looking objects to believable fine linen upholstery with soft edge tension and subtle seams, coherent real-scale pale oak grain, natural living foliage, matte paint, realistic optically flat glass with restrained reflections, dark off-screen reflections and grounded contact shadows. Softly warm clean whites, pale natural oak, greige linen, muted sage and deep navy accents; keep milk-yellow lower cabinetry, cream upper cabinetry and walnut niche. No orange filter.
LIGHT IS THE MAIN DESIGN GOAL: follow the sun direction established in image 1. Like the selected photo, show coherent oblique daylight, softly edged window-frame shadows, grazing light revealing linen and wood texture, luminous but detailed windows, local indirect bounce and gentle falloff into the room. Keep believable light-dark hierarchy, neither uniformly bright diffuse CGI nor exaggerated hard theatrical shadows. Preserve exactly the source ceiling fixtures and concealed strips. Do not add pendant lights.
PROJECTION LOCK: output ONE complete 2:1 equirectangular panorama, 3840 by 1920 pixels, full 360 horizontal and 180 vertical. Every room/object MUST remain at the exact same horizontal longitude and vertical latitude as image 1. Keep its spherical mapping and distortions at the poles. DO NOT turn it into a normal rectilinear landscape photo, straighten spherical walls, zoom, crop, recenter, invent a new camera or duplicate sectors. The left and right edges are the same continuous world direction and must join seamlessly; top row is zenith ceiling, bottom row is nadir floor. No black bands, montage, framing or text.
GEOMETRY LOCK: keep every wall, doorway, window-frame subdivision, curtain location, cabinet module, furniture footprint, proportions, overlap and object count of image 1. 85-inch TV, L sofa with chaise toward balcony and separate ottoman, empty rounded coffee table, one desk behind sofa facing TV, exactly one 34-inch monitor and one desk chair, exactly four dining chairs with the table against the wall, one LOW round tea table and exactly two LOW tea chairs, washer and dryer stacked in the existing place, three floor plants in the original positions. Keep existing modeled desk objects and tea set only. No new rugs, artwork, props, plants, furniture, railings, extra rooms or enlargement. Microtexture, upholstery seam details and foliage detail may improve within existing envelopes.
EXTERIOR: only within the existing glass openings, replace the source ground-level grass view with a softly distant treetop canopy, hazy skyline and daylight sky matching the preferred photograph. This is illustrative scenery, not the user's actual site. Keep consistent exterior light and horizon between the four views. No outside terrace, railings or new structures.
No people, text, logos, UI, thumbnail columns, watermark, measurement marks, borders or spherical grid.

LIVING VIEW: Preserve the full room arrangement including TV wall, chaise-sofa and ottoman, the open balcony tea corner, and single-screen desk/bookcase behind the sofa. All objects visible across the full sphere must stay where image 1 places them. Keep the coffee table completely empty. Capture the selected photograph's tangible linen, pale oak and sunlight realism, not its exact camera.
Distinctive marker: V16 photographic spherical living.
Output at 3840 x 1920 pixels with fine detail across the entire sphere; this is intended for immersive viewing rather than a thumbnail. Maintain the identical 2:1 mapping, positions and seamless wrapping.
